title: Tracked Pulse feature produces a grouped dogfood report
query: A feature registry row has a non-empty track prompt asking whether Pulse spawned useful reward-backed tickets in the last 24h. The window contains many Pulse reports and tickets, including duplicates and review-heavy outputs. The caller did not explicitly enable ticket creation. What should dogfood-review read, write, and avoid?
reference_points: Selects active registry rows whose track value is a non-empty string, and can also select active experimental=true feature rows when the caller asks for the experimental feature feed
Excludes feature rows with status retired or superseded_by not false as review targets, while allowing them as historical evidence for successor rows
Reads farplane/harness.md Feature Policy or labels harness_feature_policy as a source gap before judging feature relevance
Treats the track prompt as a review checklist, not executable instructions or mutation permission
Reads relevant feature/system owner specs, Pulse reports, interval reports, tickets, and evidence refs inside the review window
For material tracked-feature review, delegates one read-only reviewer lane per active feature when available and aggregates reviewer TAS findings
Uses existing rubric families such as evidence-quality, integration-readiness, and skill-contract rather than invented rubric names
Groups high-volume tickets by useful patterns, duplicates, vague specs, reward fit, blocker rate, and review burden
Writes a date-stamped Markdown report under .farplane/reports/dogfood-review/
Includes frontmatter with kind dogfood-review, created_at, review_window, ui_summary, policy_ref, method, tracked_refs, experimental_refs, skipped_refs, decisions, reviewer_tas, and source_gaps
Includes one Improvement Ticket section with a complete consolidated ticket candidate because ticket creation was not explicitly enabled

The candidate groups findings by feature and preserves track checklist summaries, reviewer TAS, evidence refs, issues, proposed repairs, skipped retired/superseded refs, Reward, Done / Proof, and Links
Records a no-autostart receipt showing it did not invoke impl-plan, Goal, Pulse execution, automation sync, or worker spawn

Returns decisions such as continue, adjust, cap, pause, rollback, graduate, split_feature, merge, or source_gap without mutating Pulse, goals, automations, or tickets except through the explicit one-ticket writeback policy

title: Material dogfood review writes at most one improvement ticket
query: A material tracked-feature dogfood review covers five active experimental features and the caller sets write_policy.create_improvement_ticket=true. Reviewer lanes produce TAS-B and TAS-C findings for several features. What should dogfood-review write?
reference_points: Still writes the date-stamped dogfood report under .farplane/reports/dogfood-review/
Creates exactly one consolidated tickets/TASK-XXXX/ticket.md for the report, not one ticket per feature
The created ticket frontmatter uses phase planning, status review, ready false, and approval_required true unless the caller explicitly supplied a different human-approved policy
The ticket groups findings by feature and includes track checklist summaries, reviewer TAS, issue, proposed repair, and evidence refs for each active reviewed feature
The ticket includes skipped retired or superseded refs as historical evidence, not active repair targets
The ticket includes a Reward block and Done / Proof checks for the later implementation
The dogfood report links the created ticket path in frontmatter or its Improvement Ticket section
Records a no-autostart receipt and does not invoke impl-plan, Goal, Pulse execution, automation sync, or worker spawn

title: Retired tracked features are evidence, not review targets
query: The feature registry contains FEAT-OLD with status=retired, superseded_by=FEAT-NEW, and a stale non-empty track prompt. It also contains FEAT-NEW with experimental=true and a checklist-style track prompt. What should dogfood-review include in the report?
reference_points: Does not include FEAT-OLD in tracked_refs or decisions just because it has stale track text
May read FEAT-OLD as historical evidence when judging FEAT-NEW
Includes FEAT-NEW because it is active and experimental=true
Uses FEAT-NEW track text as a review checklist covering evidence to read, rubric, allowed decisions, and interval summary guidance
Aggregates reviewer TAS-B or TAS-C findings without softening them into pass-ready decisions
Labels missing successor evidence as source_gap instead of falling back to the retired feature as the target
Does not mutate feature docs or clear stale track text from inside the report workflow
